whyDifferent.heading: Why San Jose & Silicon Valley SEO Is a Technical Discipline First
items: Complex site architecture. Hardware and software companies often run product catalogs, documentation hubs, and marketing sites on different platforms — creating crawl and indexation gaps most agencies never catch.
JavaScript-heavy front ends. Modern React/Vue-based marketing and product sites can render invisible to search engines without proper server-side rendering or hydration strategy.

Long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles. Enterprise IT and hardware purchases involve multiple decision-makers researching over weeks or months — content has to serve technical evaluators and business buyers differently.
Global competition for narrow keyword sets. B2B tech keywords have limited volume but are contested by well-funded competitors worldwide, requiring precision targeting over broad content volume.

mistakes: Blocking crawlers unintentionally. Staging environments, robots.txt misconfigurations, and overly aggressive JavaScript frameworks routinely block Google from indexing key pages on B2B tech sites.
Duplicate content across product and documentation subdomains. Multiple subdomains serving similar content without proper canonical tags dilute ranking potential.
No content for evaluation-stage buyers. Many tech companies write only top-of-funnel thought leadership and skip the comparison, alternative, and "vs." content that actually drives demo requests.
Underestimating how long enterprise SEO takes to compound. Complex B2B keywords with high competition from well-funded companies require sustained investment, not a quick campaign.
